releases.name: 0.11.4 — Final release: Windows lease read retry
releases.body:
# v0.11.4 — Final release: Windows lease read retry

**Final release.** This supersedes 0.11.3 as the last planned release of opencode-goal-plugin; it carries one bug fix found after 0.11.3 shipped. OpenCode ships a built-in `/goal` as of [v2.2.1](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v2.2.1); on 2.2.1 and later use the built-in command unless you need this plugin's independent verifier, limits, agent tools or multi-goal sequences. The plugin keeps working on OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 and receives bug and security fixes only. With both installed the plugin takes over `/goal`; set `commandName` to keep both (see the [README](https://github.com/william-ricchiuti/OpenCode-goal-plugin#running-alongside-the-built-in-goal)).

Install: `"plugins": ["opencode-goal-plugin@0.11.4"]` (OpenCode 2) or `"plugin": [...]` plus a `goal` command entry (OpenCode 1). [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-goal-plugin/v/0.11.4). Versions below 0.11.4 are deprecated on npm in favour of this one.

## Changes

- On Windows, retry a claim read that fails with `EPERM`, `EACCES` or `EBUSY` with the same 10 ms to 160 ms backoff as claim renames and unlinks. Windows keeps a directory entry for a claim another handle still holds open after it was unlinked and refuses to open it until that handle closes, so two plugin instances racing to reclaim a stale lease could end with the loser failing on a permission error instead of reporting the lease as contended (seen once on `windows-latest` CI, `test/persistence-lease.test.js` "simultaneous stale observers cannot both acquire the replacement lease"). The test now names the loser's error when it fails.

Everything else is as in [v0.11.3](https://github.com/william-ricchiuti/OpenCode-goal-plugin/releases/tag/v0.11.3).

releases.name: 0.11.0 — OpenCode 2 support, authoritative live leases, fail-closed verifier switching
releases.body:
# v0.11.0 — OpenCode 2 support, authoritative live leases, fail-closed verifier switching

Released on 2026-09-30. Release notes backfilled on 2026-10-30 from [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/william-ricchiuti/OpenCode-goal-plugin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

- Normalize directory separators with a linear scan, preventing adversarial location strings from causing regular-expression backtracking.
- Keep live persistence owners authoritative regardless of claim age. On OpenCode 2 location reloads, explicitly dispose the previous same-process plugin instance before initializing its replacement; do not steal a live claim on a timer.
- Fail closed when an OpenCode 2 agent switch fails or the completion verifier's identity/permissions differ from the owned definition. Revoke previously confirmed audit readiness on config conflicts, wait for the child execution before reading its verdict, and map child removal when the host exposes it.
- Make Windows-path case assertions platform-aware while preserving POSIX location isolation.
- Make the release contracts pass under npm 12 on machines whose `~/.npmrc`
  sets `allow-scripts`: `npm run` re-exports that entry as environment config,
  which npm 12 rejects with `EALLOWSCRIPTS` when the child install also passes
  `--ignore-scripts`, so the type, packed-host, and packed-tool contracts now
  strip script-policy `npm_config_*` keys from the environment they hand to
  child npm. The same three scripts also normalize npm 12's `pack --json`
  output (keyed by package name instead of a bare array): the packed-host and
  packed-tool contracts accepted only the array shape and failed at the
  install step, and the type contract crashed in its final success log even
  after both `tsc` passes because it still indexed the raw result. All three
  contracts now pass locally (`type contract passed (NodeNext + Bundler;
  opencode-goal-plugin-0.11.0.tgz)`, `packed host contract passed`,
  `packed tool contract passed … 11 tools`).
- Extend the live OpenCode 2.0.16 verification of the OpenCode 2 adapter and
  record it in `docs/compatibility.md`: command ownership over a legacy config
  `command.goal` entry on a cold boot (the plugin's framed control result is
  the admitted turn and the config template text never reaches the model), a
  full goal run to completion through `goal_complete` on a live provider, the
  auto-continue loop (two `<goal_continuation>` prompts with a live
  `<progress_budget>` countdown before the talk-only stall gate paused the
  goal), the session-title status indicator, agent registration with system
  prompts and translated permission rules, and the plugin-options precedence
  rule for a package listed in both user-level and project config.

- Add OpenCode 2 support. The default export now carries a `setup` entrypoint next to `server`: OpenCode 1 keeps reading `id` + `server` (the V1 hook map), OpenCode 2 reads `id` + `setup` and ignores `server`, so one package serves both lines and `engines.opencode` widens from `>=1.17.15 <2` to `>=1.17.15`. The new `src/v2-bridge.js` adapts OpenCode 2's plugin context onto the existing V1 hook contract instead of forking the workflow, so the goal core (state machine, persistence lease, budgets, ledger, tool surface) is unchanged: `session.hook("prompt")` drives `chat.message`, two `session.hook("context")` registrations drive `chat.params` and the system block, `session.hook("compaction")` drives `experimental.session.compacting`, `tool.hook("execute.before")` keeps the throw-to-block contract, `tool.transform`/`agent.transform` replace the `tool` map and `config` hook (Zod v4 passes through as Standard Schema, V1 agent permission/tool maps translate to ordered V2 rules with both spellings of renamed actions), `command.transform` registers `/goal` and submits the routed control result as the prompt itself, and `event.subscribe()` normalizes the V2 stream back to the V1 event shapes (`session.execution.succeeded` → `session.idle`, `…failed` →

releases.name: 0.11.3 — Final release: ledger recovery, verifier integrity, maintenance mode
releases.body:
# v0.11.3 — Final release: ledger recovery, verifier integrity, maintenance mode

> Superseded by [v0.11.4](https://github.com/william-ricchiuti/OpenCode-goal-plugin/releases/tag/v0.11.4), which adds one Windows lease fix; use that version.

**Final planned release.** OpenCode ships a built-in `/goal` as of [v2.2.1](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v2.2.1); on 2.2.1 and later use the built-in command unless you need this plugin's independent verifier, limits, agent tools or multi-goal sequences. The plugin keeps working on OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 and receives bug and security fixes only. With both installed the plugin takes over `/goal`; set `commandName` to keep both (see the [README](https://github.com/william-ricchiuti/OpenCode-goal-plugin#running-alongside-the-built-in-goal)).

Install: `"plugins": ["opencode-goal-plugin@0.11.3"]` (OpenCode 2) or `"plugin": [...]` plus a `goal` command entry (OpenCode 1). [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-goal-plugin/v/0.11.3). Verified on OpenCode 1.17.15, 2.0.16, 2.0.26 and 2.2.2.

## Changes

- Stop ledger recovery from bringing back replaced goals. Replacing a goal with `/goal <objective>`, `goal_set` or `/goal sequence` left no terminal ledger event, so after a truncated, corrupt or wrong-version `state.json` the old goal came back as a paused goal in `/goal list`. Replacements now record a `replaced` event, which recovery treats like `completed` and `cleared`. Ledgers written before this change keep the old behavior.
- Start a new ledger line when the last one was torn. A crash mid-append left a line without a newline, and the next event was appended onto it, so both were skipped as malformed and a later `cleared` or `completed` event could be lost.
- Report a ledger append as durable only when every byte was written. A short write used to count as success; the append now finishes the write or reports failure.
- Quarantine an invalid `state.json` as `state.json.corrupt.*` whenever it fails to load. It was kept only when the ledger rebuilt at least one goal; otherwise the next save overwrote it and the data was lost.
- On Windows, retry removing the persistence lease claim on release when the unlink fails with `EPERM`, `EACCES` or `EBUSY`, with the same 10 ms to 160 ms backoff as the 0.11.2 rename retry. One such failure left the instance's own claim behind, and because the owner process is always alive to itself, a same-process replacement after an OpenCode 2 location reload stayed passive until OpenCode restarted. A claim that stays locked past the retries still fails the release as before; other platforms are unchanged.
- Only affects users who set `auditorOptions.failurePolicy: "approve"`: a completion verifier whose prompt or permissions differ from the plugin's own `goal-verify` definition on OpenCode 2, or a verifier child session linked to a different parent session, was treated as an operational failure and auto-approved. These integrity failures now always reject; an unavailable API, missing child-session ID, provider error or timeout still follows the configured policy.
- Give the built-in completion verifier the whole completion claim, up to the 8000-character claim limit. It was cut to the last 1000 characters, so a structured `goal_complete` claim lost its summary and early criteria before the verifier saw it.
- Keep the recorded reason when a goal that is already stopped sees a later provider error, abort or rejected permission. A goal the assistant marked `[goal:blocked]` was relabelled `paused` with `provider error`, `user interrupted` or `permission rejected` when, for example, the turn the user spent resolving the blocker failed, so `/goal status` lost the blocker. User pauses and audit rejections were overwritten the same way.
- On OpenCode 2.2, find a goal session's existing child sessions again. 2.2 returns `session.list` as a page (`{ data, cursor }`), which the bridge did not unwrap, so `noContinueWhileChildrenActive` only saw chi

releases.name: 0.11.2 — Windows rename retry, zod security bump
releases.body:
# v0.11.2 — Windows rename retry, zod security bump

Released on 2026-10-29. Release notes backfilled on 2026-10-30 from [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/william-ricchiuti/OpenCode-goal-plugin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

- On Windows, retry the atomic rename behind goal state and persistence lease saves when it fails with `EPERM`, `EACCES` or `EBUSY`, waiting 10 ms and doubling up to 160 ms (about 0.3 s at most). Windows refuses to rename over a file another process has open, such as antivirus, an indexer or anything reading `state.json`, and one such failure on the save before an auto-continue paused the goal with `continuation claim persistence failed` until a manual `/goal resume`. In a soak that made 3% of state renames fail this way, this cut paused goals from 8 to 0. A lock that outlasts the retries still fails closed as before; other platforms are unchanged.
- Bump the pinned `zod` dependency from 4.6.5 to 4.6.7 for [GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5): earlier versions can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections (#88).

releases.name: 0.11.1 — OpenCode 2 Code Mode tool hint, lease liveness check, setup teardown
releases.body:
# v0.11.1 — OpenCode 2 Code Mode tool hint, lease liveness check, setup teardown

Released on 2026-10-18. Release notes backfilled on 2026-10-30 from [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/william-ricchiuti/OpenCode-goal-plugin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

- On OpenCode 2, tell the model where the goal tools live. OpenCode 2's Code Mode offers plugin tools only inside the `execute` tool (as `tools.goal_status()` and so on), while the plugin's prompts name the tools bare, so some models called `goal_status` directly and reported the goal tools unavailable (#85). When a request offers `execute` and no direct goal tool, the system prompt now gets a one-line note pointing the model at `execute` and the Code Mode catalog. Verified on live OpenCode 2.0.16 and 2.0.31 hosts, with the package loaded from global config as in the report: the tools were always registered in the catalog.
- Never send a liveness signal to the host's own process when checking a persistence lease owner. On Windows, runtimes that emulate POSIX signals may treat `kill(pid, 0)` as a real termination, which matches reports of the OpenCode service dying silently with the plugin installed (#81).
- On OpenCode 2, tear down everything a partially failed `setup` already started (event subscription, timers, hook registrations, and the goal core with its persistence lease) instead of leaking it on every location boot.
- On Windows, treat `/` and `\` as the same separator when matching a location, so a reload with a differently spelled path retires the previous instance instead of running beside it.
- Fix completion audits always failing on OpenCode 2.0.26. That host appends a `browser` deny rule to every agent, and the verifier ownership check compared permissions by exact JSON, so it rejected the plugin's own `goal-verify` agent and every completion was rejected. The check now accepts extra host-added deny rules, which only narrow access, and still rejects any changed, missing, reordered, allow or ask rule. Verified against live 2.0.16 and 2.0.26 hosts, including the foreign-verifier rejection mode.
- When the auditor's prompt fails and no verdict reached the transcript, report `auditor prompt failed: <reason>` instead of the misleading "no single clear final-line verdict".
